title: Evaluation des Demonstrators im Projekt ILLUMINATION (Privacy-Preserving Usage of Large Language Models in Healthcare Applications)
summary:
Patients with non-specific and/or less urgent complaints often spend long periods waiting in emergency departments without being actively involved in the care process. At the same time, physicians and nurses work under considerable time pressure. Digital tools may offer new ways to meaningfully engage patients and to collect relevant information in a structured manner.

The research project ILLUMINATION aims to develop and evaluate a digital tool that allows patients to provide a structured self-report during waiting time in the emergency department. The application uses modern language technologies (so-called Large Language Models) to guide patients through questions about their current symptoms and to provide information about emergency department processes. The goal is to support patients’ self-reflection, understanding of the situation, and preparation for the medical consultation.

The study investigates how acceptable and useful this digital tool is for patients and whether it helps them feel better informed, more oriented, and more empowered while waiting. The evaluation is conducted in several steps: first, patient expectations and needs are explored; next, an initial prototype is tested and refined; subsequently, the revised demonstrator is evaluated systematically with patients. In a final step, workshops with physicians and nursing staff explore whether the structured patient inputs could be useful for clinical work in the future.

The study focuses on feasibility and acceptance only. Medical care remains unchanged, and the collected data are not used for medical decision-making or regulatory approval processes.
conditions: This study does not investigate diseases. It is about patients who visit the emergency room due to various complaints.

interventions.name: Exploratory qualitative individual interviews with adult emergency department patients (MTS categories 3–5, triage indicator “Unwell adult”) to identify requirements, expectations, facilitating and hindering factors regarding a digital, LLM-based self-reporting tool used during waiting time in the e

Qualitative testing of an initial prototype of the digital demonstrator by adult emergency department patients in the waiting area. Assessment of subjective perceptions regarding comprehensibility, usability, perceived benefit, and acceptance using open feedback and short qualitative questionnaires.

Quantitative evaluation of the revised digital demonstrator by adult emergency department patients in the waiting area. Collection of pseudonymised usage data and standardised questionnaire data assessing perceived self-reflection, patient empowerment, preparation for the medical consultation, under

Qualitative workshops with physicians and nursing staff from the emergency department to evaluate structured summaries of patient inputs generated by the demonstrator with regard to potential clinical relevance, usability, and usefulness for anamnesis preparation and clinical decision-making.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Triage category 3–5 and MTS-indicator „Unwell Adult“
- Patient has not yet been in contact with the treating physician for his or her ED visit
Exclusion criteria:
- Incapable of giving consent (e.g., due to acute cognitive impairment, disturbance of consciousness, intoxication)
- Medical transport or admission by emergency services or doctor's office
- Insufficient German language skills for information and consent
